Review: the map so far

Thirty-nine lessons, about twenty ideas. Most of them lean on two: the return $G_t$ and the update "move an estimate a step towards a target". The value-learning methods so far differ mainly in the target they move towards.

What builds on what

Click an idea. Green ideas are what it needs, blue ideas are what it leads to. Dashed ideas are coming in units 9 and 10.

Four ways to update a value

Every value method so far fits into a square. One side asks whether the update averages over every possible next step (it needs the model $p$) or uses one sampled step. The other asks whether the target stops after one step and uses the current estimate of the next state (bootstrapping), or runs to the end of the episode. S&B draw the same square at the end of Chapter 8.

expected
(needs the model)sampled
(needs experience) one step, bootstrap to the end

The example: in state $s$ the policy picks $a$ or $b$ with probability $\tfrac12$ each. Action $a$ pays $1$ and leads to $s_1$; $b$ pays $0$ and leads to $s_2$. Current estimates $V(s) = 3$, $V(s_1) = 2$, $V(s_2) = 4$, with $\gamma = 0.9$ and $\alpha = 0.5$. One sampled episode took $b$ and ended with return $G = 2.5$.

The maths

The return is the discounted sum of future rewards (Lesson 4). Splitting off the first reward gives the recursion everything else rests on:

$$G_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma R_{t+2} + \gamma^2 R_{t+3} + \cdots = R_{t+1} + \gamma\, G_{t+1}$$

What happens from step $t$ is the next reward plus the discounted return from the step after.

A state's value under a policy $\pi$ is its expected return (Lesson 21). Taking the expectation of the recursion gives the Bellman equation (Lesson 26):

$$v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi[G_t \mid S_t = s] = \sum_a \pi(a \mid s) \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\big[r + \gamma\, v_\pi(s')\big]$$

The value of a state is the average, over actions and outcomes, of reward now plus discounted value later.

Each method turns one of these lines into an update of the form from Lesson 6:

$$V \leftarrow V + \alpha\,[\text{target} - V]$$

Only the target changes:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{DP:}\quad & V(s) \leftarrow \textstyle\sum_a \pi(a \mid s) \sum_{s',r} p(s',r \mid s,a)\big[r + \gamma V(s')\big] && (\alpha = 1)\\ \text{MC:}\quad & V(S_t) \leftarrow V(S_t) + \alpha\big[G_t - V(S_t)\big] \\ \text{TD:}\quad & V(S_t) \leftarrow V(S_t) + \alpha\big[R_{t+1} + \gamma V(S_{t+1}) - V(S_t)\big] \end{aligned}$$

DP computes the sum on the right of the Bellman equation exactly, using the model. MC replaces the expectation $\mathbb{E}_\pi[G_t]$ with one sampled $G_t$. TD, coming in Lesson 45, samples one step of the recursion and fills in the rest with its own estimate $V(S_{t+1})$.

Control follows one pattern too. Evaluate the current policy, then make it greedy with respect to the values (Lesson 34): $\pi(s) \leftarrow \arg\max_a q_\pi(s, a)$. Repeat until nothing changes.
